newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-RAINS HALTS WORLD MATCHPLAY SECOND ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-RAINS HALTS WORLD MATCHPLAY SECOND ROUND.

text.p: Heavy rain forced a halt in second-round contests at the World Matchplay golf championship on Friday, with holder Ernie Els already behind in his match.
The South African, seeking to become the first player to win three successive titles, was two down after four holes against American Steve Stricker when officials decided to stop play.
Rain had fallen for several hours and several greens on the West Course were under water when play halted at 9 a.m. (0800 GMT). Officials hoped to resume at 11 a.m. (1000 GMT).
In the other matches, Colin Montgomerie of Britain led U.S. PGA champion Mark Brooks by one hole after winning the first with a par.
U.S. Open champion Steve Jones and Fijnian Vijay Singh were on the first green when play was stopped while British Open champion Tom Lehman and fellow American Mark O'Meara had not begun.
Officials still hoped to play full 36-hole matches.
